## TL;DR

This task completed the Inputs and Context QA pass and fixed two refresh-state problems found during review. Inputs and Docs listings now use the latest request as the authority for both displayed data and the result returned to any waiting caller. Document preview loads also respect the current selection, so an older file fetch cannot replace content selected by a newer listing. Regression tests exercise both failure/success completion orders. The 375px Context capture was redeclared with a page-top anchor. The scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

The initial QA pass used headless Playwright Chromium against the auth-less dev server started from this task worktree. I checked Inputs list and board modes, an input detail drawer, the screenshot picker and preview, and Context Docs, Skills, Discover, and History at desktop and phone widths. The pages stayed within the viewport. I selected a small image, confirmed its preview, then removed the draft without submitting an input. Existing docs rendered in the Context tree and preview.

I simulated 503 responses for the Inputs and Docs listing endpoints. Before the fix, Inputs could show its successful empty state after a failed request, and Context could show “No docs found” while a request was loading or had failed. Inputs now presents a retryable error when its load fails. The docs store exposes loading and error state so Context shows loading, failure with Retry, and successful emptiness distinctly. Playwright confirmed that both pages recover after Retry.

The first concurrency fix used request versions to prevent stale responses from replacing the latest list and request flags. Review found that a stale Inputs success still returned `true` if the newest request had failed. Since `InputsView` maps the returned value to its local error banner, an older success could clear the latest failure. I changed overlapping refresh calls to resolve to the newest request’s outcome. A stale caller waits for the latest refresh result instead of guessing success from its own response. This keeps the current error visible regardless of which request finishes last.

The Docs store had a related gap after listing: an earlier `loadDocs()` could have already started `loadDoc()`, and its file fetch could finish after a newer listing selected another document. I added a separate preview-load version and selection check to `loadDoc()`. A refreshed listing now selects a valid document if the current selection disappeared, and invalidates outstanding preview work when the list becomes empty. Only the active selection may update preview title or content.

The 375px Context screenshot was previously scrolled into document content. I added a stable `context-top` anchor to the page wrapper and redeclared the narrow capture with that fragment so it opens at the initial layout. The other three Inputs/Context captures remain at their required desktop and phone viewport sizes.

## Approaches tried

For the original responsive and failure pass, I used headless Playwright and inspected viewport bounds. The first failure probe allowed a background request to recover before the assertion observed the error. I changed it to hold every matching request at 503 until Retry was pressed, making the sequence repeatable.

For the review fixes, I used deferred promises instead of timing sleeps. Tests resolve overlapping Inputs requests in both orders: an older success after a newer failure, and an older failure after a newer success. They verify the stored list and the value returned to the waiting caller. Docs tests verify that an older response cannot clear loading while the latest request is pending, and that stale success and failure do not overwrite the latest listing or error state. A separate preview test holds the older document fetch while a new listing selects another document, then resolves the old fetch last and confirms the new selection and content remain displayed.

## Challenges and blockers

The race conditions required controlling multiple requests and distinguishing list authority from the caller’s local UI state. Guarding only the data assignment did not protect `InputsView`’s error banner. Similarly, guarding `docsLoading` and `docsLoadError` did not protect preview content once `loadDoc()` had started. I addressed these as separate state channels: latest refresh promise results for callers, and a selection version for document bodies. The focused tests passed without retry or timeout behavior. No external account or physical device was needed.

The review’s screenshot note also required a useful way to express the desired scroll position. Declared capture steps support clicks, fills, waits, and hovers, but not scrolling. A page-top fragment provides a deterministic route-level anchor for the capture without relying on previously restored scroll state.

## Key learnings

Concurrent refresh correctness includes three things: which data is authoritative, which request controls shared loading/error state, and what result a caller should use for its own UI. Stale callers must observe the latest outcome rather than infer success from their own response. Preview content has a separate lifetime from the docs listing; changing the selection must invalidate older file fetches.

The focused tests passed, including the test wrapper’s boot-timing suite. The UI build/typecheck passed. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed formatting, lint, build, CSS and theme guards, rendered contrast, remote changed-path tests, branch artifact and task-asset checks, and UI smoke. The browser verification remained headless throughout.
